title: Quick Integrator Field Guide (v0)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, engineer-facing field guide for rapid integrators (internal SEs, partner engineers, and early customers) who need to wire Redwood SDK into apps and validate basic reliability and telemetry in ~30 minutes.

Audience:
- Integrator: needs minimal code + tests to go from zero to a monitored integration.
- SE/solutions: walkthrough to demo a resilient, observable SDK setup.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Provide the smallest working integration that demonstrates: auth, one text generation call, streaming, and a fallback policy.
2) Specify the minimal telemetry events and tags we must see in Console (to approve an integration).
3) Supply 6 quick smoke tests and the expected Console traces/errors.
4) List gotchas and a short troubleshooting runbook.

Quick checklist (30-min run):
- [ ] Create API key + set REDWOOD_API_KEY (or use dev token from SE account)
- [ ] Add dependency: redwood-sdk (stable) or local tarball for feature flags
- [ ] Initialize SDK with region and feature flags (see snippet)
- [ ] Run a single generation request (sync + streaming)
- [ ] Validate 3 telemetry events in Console: init, request.start, request.end or request.error
- [ ] Trigger fallback by using an explicit small-quota policy (simulated)
- [ ] Record results and paste trace link to ticket/PR

Minimal SDK init (pseudocode; pick your language):
const Redwood = require('redwood-sdk')
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  region: 'us-west-2',
  telemetry: { env: 'se-demo', sampleRate: 1.0 },
  fallbackPolicy: { fallbackTo: ['smaller-lm-v2'], maxRetries: 1 }
})

Minimal generation (sync):
resp = await client.text.generate({ model: 'open-lite-7B', prompt: 'Summarize the paragraph:' })
console.log(resp.text)

Streaming example (pseudo):
stream = client.text.stream({ model: 'open-lite-7B', prompt: 'Explain brief:' })
for await (chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk) }

Telemetry events (required fields):
- init: { client_id, sdk_version, env }
- request.start: { client_id, route, model, request_id, is_streaming }
- request.end/request.error: { request_id, latency_ms, token_count, status_code, error_code? }
- fallback.trigger: { request_id, chosen_variant, reason }
Notes: events must include a route tag (route:/api/v1/text/generate or logical route name) and a customer_id tag when available. SampleRate=1.0 for SE demos to ensure visibility.

Fallback behavior matrix (for quick test):
- Simulated out-of-quota -> fallback.trigger should fire and request completes with smaller model
- Simulated model crash (kernel OOM) -> request.error + fallback.trigger -> second request success
- Network flakey (packet drops) -> partial stream + request.error; expected user-side retry recommended

Smoke tests (commands/examples to run locally):
1) Basic sync: run node demo/sync.js -> expect HTTP 200, body.text present, Console shows request.start -> request.end.
2) Streaming: run node demo/stream.js -> expect steady chunk output, Console shows is_streaming=true.
3) Telemetry check: confirm init + start + end events within 30s in Console's traces view.
4) Fallback test: run simulate-fallback.sh (tells runtime to return 503 on primary model) -> expect fallback.trigger event + model variant in response.
5) Error propagation: run invalid-schema payload -> expect 4xx from SDK with helpful message and request.error event.
6) Cold-start latency check: restart local dev container and run 5 sequential short prompts; record p95 latency.

Expected Console signals (integration approval):
- trace link for at least one successful stream and one successful fallback
- token_count matches request size (sanity check)
- request.end latencies < 1500ms for small prompts (demo threshold)
- fallback.trigger present and annotated with reason

Support runbook (quick):
- If no init telemetry appears: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, time skew, network egress to api.redwood.ai:443.
- If requests hang during stream: check client-side TCP keepalive, proxy buffering (NGINX), and confirm SDK chunking enabled.
- If fallback never triggers: ensure admin feature flag allow_fallbacks=true for demo account.
- If console shows request.start but no end: look for killed worker (OOM) in runtime logs; request.error should appear with kernel info.

Common gotchas and anti-patterns:
- Integrators expect immediate identical behavior between hosted and private deployments. Document difference: private may enforce stricter kv-cache sizing and lower burst capacity.
- Using very large initial prompt in streaming path will artificially inflate cold-start and token billing — prefer short seed prompts during demos.
- Forgetting to set telemetry.sampleRate=1.0 for demo leads to missing traces in Console during approval.

Walking through a 15-minute demo script (recommended):
0:00 - 1:30: quick intro + set env var
1:30 - 6:00: run sync sample, show Console trace
6:00 - 9:00: run streaming demo (live output), inspect Console streaming flags
9:00 - 12:00: run fallback simulation, show fallback.trigger in trace and the alternate model returned
12:00 - 14:00: show token accounting for a run and p95 comparison
14:00 - 15:00: QA and capture notes (open PR/Confluence link)

Notes for packaging into SE kit (todo):
- Provide 3 tiny repos: node, python, and curl examples.
- A single shell script that creates an ephemeral demo API key and sets telemetry sample rate via admin API (requires a separate PR: SDK-ephemeral-keys).
- Add a lightweight grafana dashboard template (p95, errors, fallback count) and a Console saved search.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we standardize on route naming convention for integrator demos? (proposed: route:/demo/quick-integration)
- Should fallback logs include stack traces by default or only debug-level?
- What is the minimum allowed sampleRate for paid demos (privacy concerns)?

Appendix: quick troubleshooting snippets
- curl generate (minimal):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -d '{"model":"open-lite-7B","prompt":"Hello"}'

- simulate fallback (admin stub):
# toggles runtime to respond 503 for primary-model -> triggers fallback
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/runtime/simulate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"target":"open-lite-7B","action":"return_503_for_30s"}'

Record of last SE run: (placeholder)
- SE: Maya Alvarez
- Time: 2026-02-26 16:05 PST
- Results: sync success, streaming partial (proxy buffering), fallback success (model: open-micro-3B), trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-9f2b

Todo (owner tags):

End of guide (v0) — capture notes back to CONN-1245 and attach trace links before marking ready for SE kit.
